        with:

          cache: maven

        # This job absorbed the former test-reflect job, which repeated the
        # entire reactor build and differed only by -Dfastjson2.creator=reflect
        # at test time. Running the suite twice over one build halves the lane
        # count (28 -> 14), which is what relieves the runner queue.
        #
        # -Pgen-dokka is deliberately not passed. dokka resolves its ~99 MB
        # runtime tree at mojo execution time and is the sole source of every
        # cancelled lane in recent history -- 7 confirmed, all ubuntu, all
        # default-creator, all with one signature: job 111846711588 printed the
        # dokka banner at 15:52:16, then emitted nothing at all until the
        # 20-minute cap killed it at 16:07:12, leaving an orphaned java process.
        # They include job 90506607532, which cancelled the 2.0.63 release-tag
        # gate with 28 of 29 lanes green, and job 112155369041, dated after
        # #7883 merged -- so the aether timeouts in .mvn/maven.config do not
        # bound it. Dokka output is JDK- and OS-independent, so 14 lanes
        # validated nothing one lane wouldn't.
        #
        # The profile still activates on performRelease=true
        # (kotlin/pom.xml:96-101), so release builds keep generating it and the
        # published artifacts are unchanged. The trade is where a dokka break
        # surfaces: kotlin is 12th of 17 in the reactor and deploy-settings
        # binds nexus-staging:deploy per module, so a release-time dokka failure
        # strands the ~11 modules already uploaded to staging and needs a manual
        # drop. It cannot publish a broken artifact -- close is never reached,
        # and Central requires the kotlin javadoc jar that only dokka produces.
        #
        # -Pgen-javadoc stays: doclint behaviour is JDK-dependent and it has
        # never hung. Javadoc is hermetic now: the gen-javadoc profile disables
        # detectJavaApiLink and codegen no longer declares a docs.oracle.com
        # <link>, so no lane resolves external URLs. Before that, a transient
        # runner DNS fault hard-failed the 2.0.64 tag gate.
        #
        # shell: bash is required, not cosmetic. windows-latest defaults to
        # pwsh -- confirmed from a windows test lane's job log, which records
        # `shell: C:\Program Files\PowerShell\7\pwsh.EXE -command ". '{0}'"`.
        # The retry below is written in bash: `|| { ... }` and the
        # `MVNW_REPOURL=... ./mvnw` environment prefix are not pwsh syntax, so
        # the mirror fallback cannot behave as intended there. Until now all 5
        # windows test lanes ran this block under pwsh, while the windows
        # test-reflect lanes -- which did declare bash -- were the ones that
        # actually depended on the fallback.
        shell: bash
        # Retry once on failure: a stalled dependency download now fails fast
        # (see .mvn/maven.config) and the retry resumes from the partially
        # populated ~/.m2. MVNW_REPOURL lets the Maven wrapper itself fall back
        # to the GCS Maven Central mirror when repo.maven.apache.org is
        # unreachable from the runner (observed on windows-latest).
        run: |
          ./mvnw -V --no-transfer-progress -Pgen-javadoc clean package || {
            echo "::warning::Maven build failed; retrying once with the GCS Maven Central mirror as fallback"
            sleep 10
            MVNW_REPOURL=https://maven-central.storage-download.googleapis.com/maven2 ./mvnw -V --no-transfer-progress -Pgen-javadoc clean package
          }

      - name: Test again with -Dfastjson2.creator=reflect
        # Kept as its own step so a red lane still says which suite failed --
        # the job name no longer carries "Reflect" -- and so each pass's
        # duration stays visible in the job summary.
        #
        # No `clean`: this reuses the classes the previous step compiled. It has
        # to be the `test` phase, not a bare `surefire:test` goal. A bare goal
        # never runs `package` for the sibling modules, so Maven's ReactorReader
        # has no artifact to serve for them and resolution dies with "Could not
        # find artifact com.alibaba.fastjson2:fastjson2:jar:...-SNAPSHOT" even
        # though the jar is sitting in core/target/ from the previous step.
        #
        # No retry, which is a deliberate change: the former test-reflect job
        # retried its whole `clean package` on any failure, flaky tests
        # included. This pass downloads nothing new -- the previous step already
        # resolved every dependency, and this one stops at the `test` phase so it
        # never reaches the javadoc-jar binding at `package` -- so a failure here
        # is a test failure, and re-running would only delay reporting it.
        shell: bash
        run: ./mvnw -V --no-transfer-progress -Dfastjson2.creator=reflect test
